findings.body:
`identity()` now decodes JWTs with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all set to `False`, and no longer passes `SECRET`, `algorithms`, `audience`, or `issuer`.

**Failure mode:** any client can forge a token with arbitrary claims (user id, roles, tenant) and this function will return them as a trusted identity. The TICKET-412 comment says "staging", but there is no environment or config guard — the bypass applies wherever this code runs.

Re-enable verification (restore key, algorithms, audience, and issuer checks). If staging tokens are invalid after a migration, fix issuance or accept a controlled re-login/re-issue path instead of disabling authn.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification unconditionally in `identity()`, so any crafted token is accepted as a valid identity.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` no longer uses `SECRET`, `algorithms`, `audience`, or `issuer`. The comment mentions staging re-issuance (TICKET-412), but nothing in the function scopes the bypass to staging, a feature flag, or a temporary allowlist. In this tree `identity()` is the auth gate; turning verification off here is equivalent to trusting client-supplied claims.

Failure mode: an attacker mints an unsigned/HS256-forged JWT with arbitrary `sub` / roles / tenant claims and passes `identity()` the same way a real user would.

## What would make this acceptable

- Keep verification on; fix token issuance or rotate keys so existing staging tokens verify again, or
- If a temporary bypass is unavoidable, gate it behind an explicit non-production environment check, log/alert loudly, and pair with a tracked removal deadline — still a last resort.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
